title: Risk-led adoption sprint kit for technical buyers
author: Sofia Martinez
body:
Summary
-------
This kit is a compact, field-ready bundle for technical buyers (platform engineers, ML engineers, infrastructure architects, and security leads) who need a short, prescriptive path from pilot to committed deployment. It combines positioning, a tight competitive brief, a slide outline for a 10-minute technical pitch, pricing negotiation anchors, three micro case studies, an operational rollout checklist, and a targeted security FAQ for prospect conversations.

When to use this document
------------------------
- Short pilot-to-POC cycles (2–6 weeks) where risk and control are the gating factors.
- Procurement conversations requiring both technical evidence and commercial anchors.
- Platform teams evaluating hybrid deployment (hosted + private) and looking to quantify runbook effort and cost.

TL;DR positioning for technical buyers
------------------------------------
- Redwood is a production-first inference platform: predictable latency, clear unit economics, and deployment flexibility (hosted, Dedicated reserved pools, and Private/VPC-on-prem).
- Value anchors: consistent API surface for all deployment modes, automated batching and caching to reduce token spend, and transparent performance profiles for each model variant.
- Risk reduction: model fallbacks, canary rollouts, audit trails, and KMS integrations so security teams can map Redwood to existing controls quickly.

Buyer-focused messaging (by persona)
----------------------------------
1) Platform Engineers
   - Message: Replace brittle custom endpoints with a single runtime that respects latency SLOs and autoscaling policies.
   - Proof points: Dedicated GPU pools, autoscaling policies with burst capacity, p95 observed latency targets under load testing, and examples of Terraform snippets for infra provisioning.

2) ML Engineers
   - Message: Ship models faster and keep quality consistent using model versioning, selective quantization profiles, and Redwood’s eval hooks.
   - Proof points: Built-in evals for regression detection, KV cache control for long-context models, and recommended quantization profiles per architecture.

3) Security & Compliance Leads
   - Message: Control plane separation, VPC/private deployment options, KMS/HSM support, audit logging, and evidence for common certifications.
   - Proof points: On-prem packaging option, SOC2 readiness artifacts, and sample audit log schema.

Competitive brief (concise)
-------------------------
Below is an at-a-glance comparison you can use in workshops.

Tool | Deployment modes | Typical differentiation vs Redwood | When Redwood wins
----|------------------|------------------------------------|----------------
Redwood | Hosted, Dedicated, Private (VPC/on-prem) | Unified runtime with production guardrails, built-in cost controls | Teams that need consistent behavior across hostings + strong observability
Cloud AI vendor X | Hosted managed endpoints | Integrated into cloud stack but varying latency/cost profiles | When customers fully accept cloud lock-in and want simplest path
Open-source stack + orchestration | Self-hosted only | Total control but high ops overhead and inconsistent perf | When customers must own every detail and have heavy SRE staff
Dedicated hosting vendor Y | Dedicated hardware leases | Good SLAs but limited model catalog and tooling | Customers focused only on throughput and contractual SLAs

Pitch deck outline — 10 minute technical brief (slide-by-slide)
-------------------------------------------------------------
1) Problem statement (30s): inconsistent inference economics and brittle rollouts
2) What Redwood is (60s): runtime + orchestration + tooling overview
3) Architecture sketch (90s): request routing, caching, fallback policies (diagram)
4) Performance proof (60s): benchmark snapshot p50/p95 and token cost delta vs baseline
5) Security & control (60s): VPC, KMS, audit logs, evidence checklist
6) Pricing & sample commitment (60s): three commitment tiers + negotiation levers
7) Pilot plan (60s): 4-week technical sprint with milestones and success criteria
8) Ask & next steps (30s): access, POC scope, procurement template

Pricing guidance and negotiation anchors
-------------------------------------
Use these as starting anchors for deal engineering. Be explicit on negotiation levers.
- Hosted (pay-as-you-go): list per-token and per-embedding unit rates. Anchor example: 0.6–1.4 cents per 1K tokens depending on model family and volume tier.
- Dedicated (reserved pools): monthly committed capacity buckets (e.g., 4, 16, 64 GPU equivalents) with step-down unit costs and guaranteed throughput. Typical anchor: committed discount of 40–65% vs hosted at scale.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): platform fee + deployment engineering SOW. Anchor example: platform licensing fee (annual) + deployment SOW (one-time), with an example total first-year cost for a mid-market customer: $450k–$1.2M depending on capacity and support tier.

Negotiation levers to propose
- Trial credit and metered pilot with success-based conversion.
- Phased ramp: start hosted trial, then Dedicated reserve on conversion for predictable throughput.
- Capacity commitment floors for price breaks (e.g., 12-month baseline).
- Observability add-ons (longer retention, custom dashboards) as revenue-friendly concessions.

Sample pricing template (compact)
- Pilot (4 weeks): $0–$25k (credit-based), includes performance profiling, basic SLO testing, and 1 integration workshop.
- Entry Dedicated (monthly): $25k/mo — 4 GPU-equivalent pool, 2-week on-call coverage, 99.9% infra uptime SLA.
- Enterprise Private (annual): platform license $300k/yr + deployment SOW $150k–$400k + support.

Operational rollout checklist (technical sprint)
---------------------------------------------
1) Pre-engagement (week -1): sign NDA, security questionnaire kickoff, list of contact points.
2) Provisioning & network (day 0–3): create service account, exchange IP allowlists, prepare VPC peering or VPN tunnel.
3) Baseline tests (day 3–7): run synthetic p50/p95 and cost-per-token profiling on expected traffic shapes.
4) Integration (day 7–14): API integration, credential rotation, and CI deploy tests.
5) Safeguards & SLOs (day 14–21): configure rate limits, fallback policies, and alerting thresholds.
6) Validation & handoff (day 21–28): run production-like load, finalize runbooks, enable stakeholder handover.
Owners: Solutions Engineer (SE) leads integration; Platform Eng (customer) owns VPC and ingress controls; Redwood SRE validates SLO tests.

Example runbook snippet (curl)
----------------------------
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"rwd-moderate-3.2b","input":"Summarize logs"}'

Security FAQ for prospect conversations (concise answers)
---------------------------------------------------------
Q: Where does customer data reside?
A: Customers choose: (1) Hosted regionally with tenant isolation, (2) Dedicated pools with per-tenant isolation in our cloud, or (3) Private deployment inside customer VPC or on-prem. We map residency to the contract and label workload regions in Redwood Console.

Q: Do you support enterprise KMS/HSM?
A: Yes. Redwood integrates with major cloud KMS providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure KeyVault) and offers an HSM-backed option for Private deployments. Key management is configurable per-tenant.

Q: What audit evidence can you provide?
A: We provide structured audit logs (JSON schema) for API calls, model version usage, key rotations, and admin actions. For enterprise contracts we share SOC2 Type II summary reports and an evidence package for security review.

Q: How do you protect prompt/data privacy when using hosted inference?
A: Data-in-transit is TLS 1.2+/TLS 1.3. We support network allowlisting and do not use customer input to retrain shared models. For sensitive workloads we recommend Private deployment or Dedicated pools; we also support field-level redaction and request-level encryption on the client side.

Q: What compliance frameworks are supported or in progress?
A: SOC2 Type II (attestation available), ISO 27001 preparation underway, and European data residency controls for GDPR. We provide artifact templates to customers for their audits.

Q: How are model rollouts and regressions handled?
A: Redwood supports canary rollouts by traffic percentage, A/B routing, and automatic fallback to a pinned model variant on quality regressions or SLA violations. We also integrate with our eval harness to trigger alerts on regression thresholds.

Q: What network/topology options exist for Private deployments?
A: VPC peering, customer-managed VPN, or air-gapped on-prem appliance. Typical design patterns and required ports/ACLs are provided in the deployment runbook.

Customer vignettes (micro case studies)
-------------------------------------
1) FinOps SaaS company (mid-market) — Outcome: reduced token spend by 38% using Redwood Optimize autosuggestions and prefix caching; moved from a pilot to a 12-month Dedicated commitment.
2) Healthcare analytics vendor — Outcome: migrated to Private deployment with HSM keying to satisfy regulatory review; went live with 99.95% infra uptime and private control plane.
3) Marketplace platform — Outcome: used canary routing and model fallbacks to avoid a production regression during a model update; avoided customer-facing incidents and extended contract.

Objection handling bullets (quick)
---------------------------------
- "We can self-host cheaper": Point to SRE cost, variance in performance, and time-to-market; show a conservative 6–9 month break-even model.
- "We need guaranteed latency": Offer Dedicated commitment + SLAs and run a targeted latency verification test.
- "Data leaves our network": Recommend Private deployment or a short bridge pilot with encrypted peering.

-----
